title: SPARC RNEL Bladder Protocol
author: Max Novelli
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xszfnf6
materials: Anesthetize animal and maintain physiological parameters throughout procedure
Make a midline abdominal incision to expose bladder.

steps.title: Prepare Animal and Bladder Catheterization
steps.instruction: Prepare the animal for surgery and install bladder monitoring.

substeps.instruction: Place animal in the supine position.
Place tracheostomy tube and invasive blood pressure measurement catheter.
Insert dual lumen catheter into the bladder dome and secure with purse string suture and other sutures as necessary.

steps.title: Install Pelvic Nerve Cuff
steps.instruction: Identify the pelvic nerve and install the electrode cuff.

substeps.instruction: Identify and verify the pelvic nerve.
Place a 500 um nerve cuff (MicroLeads) on the left pelvic nerve.

steps.title: Close Initial Abdominal Incision
steps.instruction: Close the abdominal incision in layers using suture or staples, ensuring the catheter and electrode leads remain exposed.

steps.title: Install Pudendal and Sciatic Nerve Cuffs
steps.instruction: Expose the ischioanal fossa and install nerve cuffs on the pudendal and sciatic nerves.

substeps.instruction: Place animal in a prone position.
Make an incision on the left side just lateral to the tail to expose the ischioanal fossa.
Identify and verify the left pudendal nerve, including the sensory branch, deep perineal branch, and caudal rectal branch.
Place appropriately sized nerve cuff electrodes on all four identified pudendal nerve branches.
Place a nerve cuff (Ardiem) on the sciatic nerve ipsilateral to the other nerve cuffs.

steps.title: Close Second Incision
steps.instruction: Close the incision with suture or staples.

steps.title: Perform Laminectomy and Install Spinal Array
steps.instruction: Expose the spinal cord and place the stimulation array.

substeps.instruction: Mark the dorsal process location with suture.
Perform laminectomy by removing the L6, L7, and S1 lamina.
Place a 16 or 24 channel epidural spinal cord array (MicroLeads) on the spinal cord.

steps.title: Align Epidural Stimulation Array
steps.instruction: Align the array based on the chosen stimulation location.

substeps.instruction: For the most rostral location: align the most rostral row of electrodes to the center L6 process.
For the more caudal locations: align the most caudal row of electrodes to the L7 or S1 spinous processes, respectively.

steps.title: Connect Hardware and Software
steps.instruction: Connect electrodes to headstages and configure the stimulation system.

substeps.instruction: Connect nerve cuff electrode contacts to the recording headstage.
Connect epidural stimulation array contacts to the stimulation headstage.
Use a Grapevine Neural Interface Processor through a Nano 2+Stim high-current headstage, controlled by MATLAB (Mathworks) XippMex API.

steps.title: Configure Stimulation Pulse Parameters
steps.instruction: Set the asymmetric charge-balanced pulses with the following parameters: 200 us cathodal phase, 66 us interphase period, and 400 us anodal phase at half the current amplitude.

steps.title: Perform Initial High-Amplitude Survey
steps.instruction: Identify responsive electrodes using a high-amplitude, low-frequency survey.

substeps.instruction: Deliver 50 stimulation pulses to all electrodes, one at a time, in random order.
Set frequency to 20 Hz and current amplitude typically between 400-800 uA (empirically determined via test pulse trains to activate the sciatic nerve and most other cuffs).
Observe the longest-latency responses and add 5 ms to determine the minimum response latency of interest for a given electrode.

steps.title: Process Nerve Cuff Recordings
steps.instruction: Clean and analyze the recorded data.

substeps.instruction: Remove stimulus artifact.
High-pass filter the data.
Perform stimulus-triggered averaging to find mean nerve responses.

steps.title: Verify Compound Action Potentials (CAP)
steps.instruction: Determine the presence of a CAP on each nerve by comparing stimulation-triggered averages to baseline recordings without stimulation.

steps.title: Determine Threshold Stimulus Amplitudes
steps.instruction: Identify the minimum current required to recruit activity on each nerve using a binary search procedure.

substeps.instruction: Include electrodes that produced CAPs on the pelvic and pudendal nerves.
Use the stimulation frequency determined by the minimum response latency from the initial survey.
Apply a binary search algorithm for each electrode to find the minimum stimulus threshold for a detectable response in each instrumented nerve.
Average typically 300 individual stimulus pulses.

steps.title: Apply Electrode Configurations
steps.instruction: Localize current below the electrodes using different configurations.

substeps.instruction: Apply stimulation to monopolar configurations.
Apply stimulation to multipolar configurations, including bipolar (two adjacent electrodes horizontally or vertically) and tripolar (adjacent vertical electrodes) sets.
